extra.message: User-controlled input from request.GET['expr'] is passed directly to eval(). An attacker can execute arbitrary Python code by providing a malicious expression like '__import__(\"os\").system(\"id\")'. This allows full remote code execution.

User-controlled data from request.body or request.GET['blob'] is passed to pickle.loads() without validation. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload to execute arbitrary code during deserialization. This is a critical remote code execution vulnerability.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is concatenated into a Jinja2 template and rendered server-side. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax to achieve server-side template injection (SSTI), leading to arbitrary code execution.

User-controlled input from request.GET['packet_ref'] is used to construct a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences like '../../../etc/passwd' to read arbitrary files on the filesystem.

User-controlled URL from request.GET['url'] is passed to urllib.request.urlopen() without validation. An attacker can make the server request internal resources (SSRF), accessing services like cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) or internal APIs.

XML parser is configured with resolve_entities=True and no_network=False, enabling XML External Entity (XXE) attacks. An attacker can provide malicious XML with external entity references to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled data from request.body is parsed as JSON and passed directly to MongoDB find_one() query. An attacker can inject NoSQL operators like {'$ne': null} or {'$where': '...'} to bypass authentication or extract data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The code creates an unverified SSL context using ssl._create_unverified_context(), which disables certificate validation. This makes the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

User-controlled input from request.GET['marker'] is set directly as a cookie value without sanitization. An attacker can inject HTTP header sequences like '\r\n' to manipulate response headers or set arbitrary cookies.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header reflects the user-provided Origin header without validation. Combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, this allows any malicious website to make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of users.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The code explicitly disables XSS protection (X-XSS-Protection: 0) and clears Content-Security-Policy header. This weakens browser security controls and increases the risk of XSS attacks succeeding.
